chosen.premise: At just 3.2 kg, Weedle eats its own body weight in leaves every single day.
chosen.hook: This tiny Pokémon eats 3.2 kilos of leaves a day.
chosen.visualIdea: A 3.2 kg Weedle stands beside a leaf pile that rises until it matches its entire body weight.
chosen.note: A highly concrete daily-feeding claim uniquely tied to Weedle, with the 3.2 kg weight and Pokédex statement directly supporting the comparison.

candidates.premise: Weedle chooses favorite leaves by smell, using its big red proboscis to reject the rest.
candidates.hook: Weedle can smell which leaves it actually likes.
candidates.visualIdea: Weedle sniffs a lineup of leaves; favorites light up green while disliked leaves get pushed aside.
candidates.note: Weedle’s ability to distinguish preferred leaves by smell is unusually specific and well supported; the proboscis-based visual makes the mechanism clear.

candidates.premise: Weedle's defense is a roughly two-inch toxic barb growing from the top of its head.
candidates.hook: Weedle has a poison barb sticking out of its head.
candidates.visualIdea: A ruler snaps beside Weedle's head barb, then the barb glows as an attacker backs away.
candidates.note: The exact two-inch measurement and head location are strongly supported and easy to demonstrate, though poison stingers are broadly familiar to Pokémon fans.

candidates.premise: The leaf-eating Weedle becomes Kakuna at level 7, then a Beedrill only three levels later.
candidates.hook: Weedle's final evolution is only three levels after Kakuna.
candidates.visualIdea: A level meter hits 7 for Weedle-to-Kakuna, then races just three more ticks to reveal Beedrill.
candidates.note: The level-7-to-level-10 progression is concrete and visually strong, but the cited Pokédex evidence is partly irrelevant and the three-level gap alone is not an especially rich premise.

candidates.premise: Weedle eats leaves, hides under those same leaves, and emerges with a toxic head barb.
candidates.hook: Weedle hides underneath the food it eats.
candidates.visualIdea: A leaf pile rustles: first a red nose appears, then Weedle emerges and raises its toxic head barb.
candidates.note: The Pokédex supports Weedle hiding under leaves it eats and having a toxic barb, but “those same leaves” and the emergence sequence are slightly interpretive.

candidates.premise: Weedle's bright body warns enemies away—but it also carries a powerful poison stinger.
candidates.hook: Weedle's colors are a warning label.
candidates.visualIdea: Weedle's bright body becomes a flashing warning sign, followed by a close-up of its poison-tipped barb.
candidates.note: The research supports both warning coloration and a powerful poison barb, but the premise is a fairly general profile rather than a sharply distinctive angle.

rounds.request: A stronger angle would need a more surprising Weedle-specific rule or contradiction than the current candidates, ideally combining an exact measurable fact with a distinctive behavior and direct first-party support.
